dedupe_keys.name: epa waste estimation support tool west for radiological incidents

description: The Waste Estimation Support Tool (WEST) estimates the volume and radioactivity of the waste that would be generated by a radiological dispersal device incident and by the decontamination and demolition that follow. It was developed by the US Environmental Protection Agency's homeland security research programme to support a systems approach to wide-area remediation, in which waste management is planned together with cleanup. WEST combines ArcGIS scripts that define the contaminated area and level of contamination, FEMA Hazus software that estimates building counts, floor area and construction, applications that identify outdoor surfaces from satellite imagery, and an Excel workbook that estimates the quantity and characteristics of the waste and compares remediation strategies. Coverage is any US area. WEST is a free download from EPA; as a US government work it is public domain, though it needs ArcGIS and Hazus. Caveats: it gives first-order planning estimates, depends on assumed contamination and decontamination efficiency, and addresses radiological incidents only. Simulation uses: waste quantities for disaster waste logistics and recovery models of wide-area contamination. Related records: the EPA All Hazards Waste Logistics Tool (model-epa-all-hazards-waste-logistics-tool) can route the estimated waste.
